Hi, I’m Hanaa.

I’m a content creator and digital marketer in Cairo. I create Arabic and English content for ENAN in Iraq, and I started my career as a front-end developer.

Before marketing I built websites, so I write with the page in mind: how fast it loads, how easy it reads, and what makes someone act. I have also written, designed, and published social posts for BioMarine, a skincare brand in Iraq.

ENAN: making “managed operations” something you can picture

Motion-graphics reels · Arabic · Creative direction

ENAN sells a service that is hard to see. Each reel takes one everyday image and one message, in the brand’s black and gold.

GPS: a lost arrow, three dead ends, then a clear route through five steps. “You decide the destination, we walk the road.”

Scale: promises pile up until one small gold ball, a weekly report, tips it. “Execution is what weighs.”

I directed the concepts, sent back a draft that repeated itself, picked the typography, and applied the 2026 identity. The reels were built with Claude and code, with no stock footage.

Concept project

A strategy I built from scratch for a brand I don’t work with, to show how I plan.

Eva Egyptian Treasures: every product has a hometown

Content strategy · Skincare and haircare · Egypt · Self-initiated, not commissioned by or affiliated with Eva Cosmetics

The story already exists

The line uses local ingredients like spirulina, rice water, hibiscus, and papyrus extract, with no sulfates, parabens, or silicones. Every pack has a QR code that leads to the region its ingredients come from.

My idea

Turn that into a series. Each post follows one ingredient back to its hometown, so the QR code starts a story instead of sitting on the back of the pack.

Three pillars

  • Ingredient stories: one ingredient, one place, one benefit.
  • Clean label, explained: what “no sulfates, parabens, or silicones” means, in plain Arabic.
  • Routine habits: how to use the hair bars and why packageless works.

Who it’s for (my hypothesis)

Egyptian women who read ingredient lists and like knowing where things come from. I would test this against the brand’s audience data first.

What I noticed on Eva’s Instagram (a snapshot from November 2026)

  • The page has about 370K followers and 1,182 posts. Of the five posts I reviewed, three were offers, one announced an award, and one was a breast cancer awareness collaboration. The top of the grid was an award post followed by four Green Friday offers.
  • Likes on those five posts ranged from 34 to 593, roughly 0.01% to 0.16% of followers. That counts likes only, on five posts, so it is a snapshot and not a verdict. The free tinted sunscreen gift got the most.
  • Under the buy-two-get-one post, one person asked for prices and another asked for a splash she could not find online, in pharmacies, or in markets. Both comments have a reply.
  • The offers send people to three mall branches, and the bio links to the online shop. The Highlights are organized around events: a Noon event, Ramadan, and Christmas.
  • The Egyptian Treasures hometown story did not appear in the posts I reviewed.

Three competitors, same snapshot

BrandFollowersWhat the feed doesWhere to buy
Eva370KMostly offers and company news, with event-based HighlightsOffers name three mall branches; the bio links to the shop
Shaan252KOne emotional campaign line, “take a minute for yourself”, in a consistent pink look with real facesNot in the captions I saw; the bio links to a retailer page
Raw African435KHumor-led video, kids’ product launches, and offers; Highlights such as HairGuide, Reviews, and Special OffersOffers list eight booth locations; captions in English and Arabic
Hathor17.5KEgyptian heritage: the bio says “5000 years in the making”, with hieroglyph imagery, long ingredient explanations, and a before-and-after story; both captions I saw were in EnglishWebsite link in the bio and a “Find Us Here” Highlight
  • Story-led video drew far more attention than offers. Raw African’s humorous hair video from January shows over 2,300 likes, while its two Black Friday offers, a few days old, show 22 and 23. The ages differ, so it is not a fair race, but the gap is large.
  • Under that same video, people asked what the product does, how to use it, and what it costs. Comments under Eva’s and Hathor’s posts asked about price as well.
  • Shaan’s two recent posts show 59 likes (one day old) and 291 (five days old). Its strength is one campaign line used consistently.
  • Hathor is the one that builds on Egyptian heritage, but it is small, and in the two posts I reviewed it explains ingredients rather than telling where each one comes from. The other two did not tell an ingredient-origin story in the posts I reviewed.

What that changes

The feed is built for offers and company news, so my series would not replace it. It adds a story layer that gives followers a reason to care before the next promotion. Because people ask what things cost and where to find them, every post would end with where to buy, and I would add a “hometowns” Highlight beside the event ones. The competitor posts add two lessons: storytelling earns more attention than offers, and each post should answer something practical, such as what the product does or how to use it, not only create a feeling. Hathor already uses Egyptian heritage on a small scale, so my version leans on what is different: a mass-market brand, plain Arabic copy, and sources you can trace through the QR code.

Four-week plan and how I’d measure it
Week 1Introduce the idea with a map reel.
Week 2Two ingredient stories as carousels.
Week 3Clean-label explainer and a myth-or-fact post.
Week 4Hair bar reel and a call for followers’ routines.

I would track saves and shares on carousels, replies on the reel, and QR scans, which only the brand can see.

Instagram observations come from the public pages of Eva, Shaan, Raw African, and Hathor in November 2026. Product details come from Elle Egypt’s feature on the line and Eva’s app listing. A real project would start with the brand’s guidelines and audience data, and would review competitors in more depth.
